# Add an interactive hierarchy widget to a plotly plot

Adds a draggable, resizable hierarchy widget to a line plot of a
hierarchical or grouped time series made with
[`plotly::ggplotly()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/plotly/man/ggplotly.html).
Levels can be reordered by dragging and toggled by clicking, and the
traces are restyled accordingly.

## Usage

``` r
add_hierarchy_plotly(plot, structure, width = NULL, height = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- plot:

  A plotly htmlwidget returned by
  [`plotly::ggplotly()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/plotly/man/ggplotly.html).

- structure:

  Aggregation structure as a string, such as `"(State/Region)*Purpose"`.

- width, height:

  Output size (any valid CSS unit). When omitted, the original plotly
  dimensions and sizing policy are kept.

## Value

The plotly htmlwidget with the hierarchy widget attached.

## Details

Each trace must identify its series through its hover text, in the form
`"State: Tasmania<br>Region: Hobart and the South<br>Purpose: Holiday"`,
with `<aggregated>` for aggregated levels.

## See also

[`add_hierarchy_hc()`](https://yvesypher.github.io/ggelato/reference/add_hierarchy_hc.md)

## Examples

``` r
library(ggplot2)

tas_hts <- fabletools::aggregate_key(
  aus_tourism[aus_tourism$State == "Tasmania", ],
  (State / Region) * Purpose,
  Trips = sum(Trips)
)
tas_hts$series <- paste0(
  "State: ", tas_hts$State, "<br>Region: ", tas_hts$Region,
  "<br>Purpose: ", tas_hts$Purpose
)

tas_plot <- ggplot(
  as.data.frame(tas_hts),
  aes(
    x = as.Date(Quarter), y = Trips,
    group = series, text = series
  )
) +
  geom_line()
add_hierarchy_plotly(
  plotly::ggplotly(tas_plot, tooltip = "text"),
  "(State/Region)*Purpose"
)
```
